Convert industry codes between DB07 and DB25 using Statistics Denmark's keys

Source: R/convert_db07_to_db25.R
convert_db07_to_db25.Rd

Converts full six-digit codes in either direction using a bundled copy of Statistics Denmark's correspondence table (source page updated 26 February 2026, downloaded 24 October 2026). No network connection is needed at runtime. Dots and whitespace are handled automatically, including mixed input.

Usage

convert_db07_to_db25(
  x,
  format = c("dotted", "compact"),
  method = c("strict", "simple")
)

convert_db25_to_db07(
  x,
  format = c("dotted", "compact"),
  method = c("strict", "simple")
)

Source

Statistics Denmark: DB25 and conversion tables. The rebuild script data-raw/db07_db25.R records the source file URLs.

Arguments

x

A vector of full codes in the source classification, coerced to character if needed.

format

Output format: "dotted" (default) or "compact".

method

"strict" (default) converts only codes with a single destination. "simple" uses DST's simplified conversion matrix.

Value

A character vector of the same length and order as x.

Details

convert_db07_to_db25() converts DB07 to DB25; convert_db25_to_db07() converts DB25 to DB07. The input classification must be chosen explicitly: the same code can occur in both classifications with different meanings.

With method = "strict", codes with multiple destinations return NA with a warning. With method = "simple", the destination is taken from DST's separate simplified conversion matrix for the chosen direction. The reverse conversion does not invert the forward simplified matrix. This is an approximation: DST bases the choice on numbers of units, not economic activity. It cannot establish the correct code for every individual business or allocate turnover between split industries.

Input must contain exactly six digits after removing dots and whitespace and must occur in the source classification's key. Invalid lengths, unknown codes, and other characters return NA with a warning. Missing input remains NA without a warning. Leading zeroes are never guessed; keep codes as character data. Aggregated codes are not supported.

See also

format_db07()

Examples

convert_db07_to_db25(c("011100", "01.49.10", NA))
#> [1] "01.11.00" "01.48.00" NA        
convert_db07_to_db25("01.19.00", method = "simple", format = "compact")
#> [1] "011900"
convert_db25_to_db07("25.30.00", format = "compact")
#> [1] "254000"
# df |> dplyr::mutate(db25 = convert_db07_to_db25(db07))
